title: Activation ownership timetable and risk fuse
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, actionable timetable for owner-level responsibilities during the first 72h of a major product activation (internal beta -> public ramp). It pairs a minute-to-hour ownership cadence with KPI thresholds we call the ‘risk fuse’ — explicit triggers that force pre-planned mitigations (traffic caps, model downgrade, extra oncall).

TL;DR (one-line):
Map people -> windows -> KPIs -> fuse thresholds -> immediate actions. Keep this doc pinned to the activation channel and the on-call dashboard.

Core concepts (short):
- Ownership timetable: who owns which operational window (minutes/hours) and which KPIs they monitor.
- Risk fuse: a small set of thresholded signals (latency P95, error % by route, cost burn rate, user-facing error rate) that, when tripped, must trigger the listed mitigation within X minutes.
- Micro-runbooks: bite-sized action steps mapped to each fuse state (monitor, warn, throttle, rollback).
- Surge staffing: pre-committed roles ready to jump in with exact scopes (SRE triage, Model Ops fallback, Customer Success comms).

Activation windows and owners (72h):
- Hour 0-3 (Immediate handoff): Owner: Maya Patel (Product Ops lead). Watch: request success %, P50/P95 latency, token burn spike. Fuse thresholds: error% > 1.5% for 5m OR P95 > 1.2s for 3m -> Action: enable routing to canary model variant, page SRE.
- Hour 3-12 (Stabilization): Owner: Carlos Rivera (SRE lead). Watch: queue length, retry rate, downstream DB errors. Fuse: queue > 2500 OR retry > 4% for 10m -> Action: open capacity burst (Dedicated pool), temporarily reduce batch sizes, notify Product.
- Hour 12-36 (Scale test): Owner: Aisha Khan (Product Ops manager). Watch: adoption cohort conversion, per-user token spend, infra cost burn vs expected. Fuse: cost burn > 140% of forecast for 6h -> Action: enable cost throttle (limiter per-api-key), notify finance and sales for customer calls.
- Hour 36-72 (Normalization): Owner: Tom Beattie (Release engineer). Watch: regression in model quality (eval prompts), 5xxs trending up. Fuse: regression AUC drop > 3% on sentinel set OR 5xx > 0.7% -> Action: initiate rollback to previous model snapshot, start postmortem thread.

KPIs to surface on the launch deck (minimum):
- Latency: P50, P95, P99 per-route and per-region (ms).
- Reliability: 4xx/5xx rates, request success % by route.
- Throughput: RPS sustained and burst, queue depth.
- Economic: tokens generated per minute, cost burn vs forecast (USD/hour).
- Quality: eval pass rate on prompt set, manual customer-reported regression count.

Risk fuse (concrete thresholds):
- Latency fuse: P95 delta > +40% vs baseline for 5m -> Warn. P95 > 1.2s -> Fuse tripped.
- Error fuse: 5xx rate > 0.5% for 3m -> Warn. 5xx rate > 1.5% for 5m -> Fuse tripped.
- Cost fuse: burn vs forecast > 120% sustained for 4h -> Warn. > 140% for 6h -> Fuse tripped.
- Quality fuse: evaluation fail rate increase > 2% absolute on sentinel prompts -> Fuse tripped.

Immediate mitigations (micro-runbooks):
- Warn state: owner posts in #activation-channel, updates the deck, calls the on-call lead for triage.
- Throttle state: enable per-key rate-limiter (Config path: /configs/rlimit/activation) and reduce burst to 50% for new traffic.
- Fallback state: switch traffic to compatible model variant (tag: "stable-2026-01"), enable read-only cache mode for long sequences, set maintenance banner for heavy-traffic customers.
- Rollback state: revert to pinned model snapshot (model_id: rollback-target-2026-01), drain new deployments, and run immediate postmortem schedule.

Surge staffing roster (pre-committed):
- SRE triage (Carlos Rivera): minutes -> hour 1 response, owns infra scaling calls.
- Model Ops on-call (Nikhil Desai): ready to flip routing/quantization profile, owns model rollback.
- Customer Success comms (Lina Park): ready to send templated messages to beta customers and coordinate support.
- Finance point (Ravi Shah): approve temporary cost buffers and advise on cost throttle policy.
- Incident facilitator (Maya Patel): coordinates cross-team decision and timeline.

Preflight checklist (before traffic unthrottle):
- All owners introduced in kickoff (yes/no).
- Canary traffic passed 24h smoke: success% > 99.5 and P95 within 10% of baseline.
- Sentinel evals green (no regressions > 1% in last 48h).
- Rollback snapshot verified and tested on staging.
- Escalation contact list pinned to the deck and Slack channel.

Decision record examples (how to decide to throttle vs rollback):
- If 5xx spike confined to a single region and latency stable => region isolate + route away (no rollback).
- If global model quality regressions detected on sentinel set AND customer-facing errors > 0.5% => immediate rollback.
- If cost burn rises but no error/latency signals => apply cost throttle and open finance/sales sync; only rollback if cost throttle insufficient within 4h.

Post-activation followups (owners & SLAs):
- 24h: SRE-led triage summary posted (owner: Carlos) with actions and lingering risk items.
- 72h: Product Ops post-mortem draft (owner: Maya) + metrics appendix (latency, errors, cost).
- 7d: Final report with customer impact and recommended runway changes (owner: Aisha).

Appendix: quick templates to paste into Slack/email
- Slack alert template (page): "[ALERT] <fuse> tripped on <route>. Owner <name> taking action <action>. Current: P95=<val>, 5xx=<val>%. Paging SRE + ModelOps."
- Customer comms snippet: "We're investigating elevated errors during your session window. We're actively rolling back to a stable model and will follow up in <1h>."

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm finance buffer pre-approval for cost spikes > 140% (assigned: Ravi).
- Add endpoint-level KPIs to dashboard (assign: Observability team ticket OPS-4123).
- Dry-run the timetable in next internal scale exercise (owner: Product Ops).

How to use this doc in practice:
- Paste the ownership table into the launch deck; keep the risk fuse section near the top of the operational playbook; use KPI thresholds to bind decisions rather than debate.

Last notes: this is intentionally terse — the goal is a single-pane decision guide that people can act from in minutes. If you’re listed as an owner, know your page tree and the exact command to flip the switch in the runbook (link: confluence:PRODOPS-7864).

Revision log (brief):
- 2025-11-03 created by Maya Patel (initial draft).
- 2025-12-01 updated thresholds after scale test (Carlos).
- 2026-02-20 minor wording and added surge roster (Aisha).
